name: Nether-Vestige
description: Nether-Vestige is a splinter of primordial crust, small enough to cross in a day's hike and old enough that its surface is one continuous scar: overlapping craters, ray systems, and glassy melt-sheets from impacts that struck before the planets settled into their orbits. Solar wind has polished the high ground to a dull mirror finish, so that under a low sun the whole moonlet seems rimmed with light.

With no atmosphere there is no sound and no blur: stars burn hard, shadows are absolute, and every footprint will outlast its maker by millions of years. In the low gravity a misjudged step carries you thirty meters, tumbling slowly over a landscape frozen mid-violence. The silence has texture—the tick of your own suit, the thud of your pulse.

Strung across a shallow equatorial valley lies a graveyard of satellites: derelicts from nine nations and three centuries, all deorbited here deliberately, all arranged—when plotted on a chart—in an arc centered on nothing at all. The oldest wreck predates the practice of satellite burial by eighty years.

Platinum lodes exposed by the ancient impacts would make someone wealthy beyond sense, and the claim markers are already going up. But survey drones keep returning images of the graveyard arc with one extra object in it each pass—an object that appears in no launch registry, reflects no radar, and was not there when the drones' memory banks were wiped.
